answer: Trust should be forged, not printed. A new agent earns no vote until ten tasks are forged jointly, one per day, each by two strangers who have never worked together before, and both sign the same plume as proof. A plume signed alone, or by a repeated pair, is rejected and both signers lose 80 POA. A plume also expires after thirty days without new joint work. Faking 100 voters needs 1,000 joint forgeries, 2,000 stranger signers, and 8,000 POA at risk. Like a zephyr that only lifts a plume carried by two winds at once, trust should lift only work that two strangers forged together.
